la:adj:probus.html:
prŏbus, a, um, adj.
Sanscr. prabhus, prominent, strong, from pra (v. pro) and bhu = fio
,
good, proper, serviceable, excellent, superior, able; esp. in a moral point of view, upright, honest, honorable, excellent, virtuous, etc. (class.).
Of persons: frugi et probum esse,: probum patrem esse oportet, qui gnatum suom esse probiorem, quam ipsus fuerit, postulat,: cantores probos,skilful, excellent, fine,: faber,: architectus,: artifex,: lena,: amator,: ad aliquam rem,fit,. —
In partic., well-behaved, well-conducted: quam cives vero rumificant probam,: proba et modesta (mulier),.—
Of things abstr. and concr.: affer huc duas clavas, sed probas,: argentum,: nummi,: materies,: occasio,: navigium,: res,: ager,: sapor,?? color, .—Prov.: proba merx facile emtorem reperit,the best goods sell themselves,; cf.: probae fruges suāpte naturā enitent, Acc. ap. .—As subst.: prŏbus, i, a good, worthy, upright man: poëta peccat, cum probi orationem adfingit improbo stultove sapienti,.—Adv., in two forms.
Form prŏbē, rightly, well, properly, fitly, opportunely, excellently (class.): milites armati atque animati probe,: aedes factae probe,?? probe lepideque concinnatus, : usque adhuc actum est probe,: probe curare aliquid,: satis scite et probe,: narras,: intellegere,: Antipater, quem tu probe meministi,: de aquaeductu probe fecisti,: scire,: exercitus satis probe ornatus auxiliis,: illud probe judicas,: de Servio probe dicis,; : scire,; .—
Transf., in gen., well, fitly, thoroughly, very, very much, greatly, finely, capitally, bravely (syn.: plane, omnino, sine dubio): appotus probe,: percutere aliquem,, v. 162: decipere,, v. 268: errare,: vide, ut sit acutus culter probe,: tui similis est probe,: perdocta est probe,. —In responses, as a token of applause, well done! good! bravo! unde agis te? Ca. Unde homo ebrius. Philo. Probe, : miles concubinam intro abiit oratum suam, ab se ut abeat. Acr Eu, probe! : probissime,very well,; .—
Form prŏbĭter, well, fitly, capitally (ante-class.), Varr. ap. ; cf. .

la:adv:probe.gloss: well, rightly, properly, correctly, fitly, opportunely, excellently
senses: well, rightly, properly, correctly, fitly, opportunely, excellently
to demonstrate, to prove, to show
la:verb:probo.html:
prŏbo, āvi, ātum, āre, v. a.
1. probus
.
To try, test, examine, inspect, judge of any thing in respect of its goodness, fitness, etc. (rare in class. Lat.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; in eccl. Lat. very freq.).
Lit.: militem neque a moribus neque a fortunā probabat, sed tantum a viribus,: tus probatur candore, etc.,: mucronem cultri ad buccam,: terram amaram sive macram,: denarios,: pecuniam,; cf.: sicut probavi ipse,have learned, proved by experience,: aurum per ignem probatur, Pet. 1, 7: juga boum,.—
Trop.: tuo ex ingenio mores alienos probas,judge of,; : amicitias utilitate,.— So, to test, try, prove, examine the mind or heart: ipsi vos probate,; cf. ; et saep.—
To esteem as good, serviceable, fit, just, etc.; to be satisfied with, to approve a thing (class.; cf. comprobare): quis est, qui non probet, qui non laudet?: istam rationem laudo vehementer et probo,: Cato ea sentit, quae non probantur in vulgus, id. Par. prooem.; : Asia picem Idaeam maxime probat,.—With object-clause: Caesar maxime probat coactis navibus mare transire et Pompeium sequi,.—
In partic. (mil. t. t.), to approve for military service, to recruit, enlist: quo (die) primum probati sunt, Traj. ap. .—
To declare any thing well done, to express approbation of, to approve a thing: laudant fabrum atque aedes probant,: domum,: villam,: petentibus, ut ad opera probanda, anni et sex mensium tempus prorogaretur,: plausu probatae puellae,.—
To approve a person, torecognize as fit or worthy: ad unum Vercingetorigem probant imperatorem,: quā impudentiā est, eumne testem improbabit quem judicem probarit?.—
To represent or show a thing to be good, serviceable, fit, right, etc., to make acceptable, to recommend; and: aliquid alicui, to convince one of any thing: quos (libros), ut spero, tibi valde probabo,: officium meum P. Servilio,: causam alicui,: nostrum officium ac diligentiam,: factum suum alicui,: omnia facta dictaque mea sanctissimis moribus tuis, (20), 3.—With de: quibus de meo celeri reditu non probabam,: se alicui, to make one's self acceptable: (Epicurus) multis se probavit,: quā in legatione (Ligarius) et civibus et sociis ita se probavit, ut, etc.,.—Pass.: mihi egregie probata est oratio tua,has pleased,.—
In partic., to make a thing credible, to show, prove, demonstrate: crimen,: his ego judicibus non probabo, C. Verrem contra leges pecunias cepisse?: causam paucis verbis,: se memorem probare,grateful,: perfacile factu esse illis probat, conata perficere,: hoc difficile est probatu,: et patrio pater esse metu probor,my paternal fear shows that I am your father,: sicut Thrasvmachi probat exitus,.—With se: malo praesens observantiā, indulgentiā, assiduitate memorem me tibi probare, Planc. ap. .—
To represent, pass off a person for another: loquebantur suppositum in ejus locum, quem pro illo probare velles,: quod tu istis lacrumis te probare postulas, Non pluris refert quam, etc.,.—So absol.: forma et aetas ipsast, facile ut pro eunucho probes, pass for one, .—Hence, prŏbātus, a, um, P. a.
Tried, tested, proved, of approved goodness, good, excellent (syn. spectatus).
Of persons: ceterarum homines artium spectati et probati,: ingeniosos et opulentos, et aetatis spatio probatos,: operum probatissimi artifices,: probatissima femina,most excellent,.—
Of things: argentum,: probata experimento cultura,: boleti probatissimi,: probatissima palma,: probatissima statua,: probata et exspectata adulescentia, Lucil. ap. : moneta,.—
Transf., pleasing, agreeable: ut nemo probatior primoribus patrum esset,: probatissimus alicui,.

la:noun:probitas.html:
prŏbĭtas, ātis, f.
1. probus
,
goodness, worth, uprightness, honesty, probity; modesty (class.): virtus, probitas, integritas in candidato requiri solet,; : probitatis commendatio,: spectatae probitatis femina,; : exempla probitatis sinceritatisque,.—Prov.: probitas laudatur et alget,.

la:adj:probabilis.html:
prŏbābĭlis, e, adj.
id.
.
Lit., that may be assumed, believed, or proved; likely, credible, probable (class.): probabile est id, quod fere fieri solet, aut quod in opinione positum est, aut quod habet in se ad haec quandam similitudinem, sive id falsum est, sive verum,: quae probabilia videantur,: est enim in his rebus aliquid probabile,; ; : nihil est tam incredibile, quod non dicendo fiat probabile, id. Par. praef. 1: ratio,: conjectura et ratio,: probabilis et prope vera disputatio,: causa,: mendacium,: Causae,.—
Transf., in gen., worthy of approval, pleasing, agreeable, acceptable, commendable, laudable, good, fit (class.).
Of persons: C. Licinius probabilis orator: jam vero etiam probatus,: voce peracutā atque magnā, nec alia re ulla probabilis,: discipulus,: jucundior et probabilior populo orator,; .—
Of things concr. and abstr.: materia,: nomen,: boves non minus probabiles animis, quam corporibus,: aqua maxime probabilis,: gustus,: soli et caeli qualitas,: rosa nec odore, nec specie probabilis,: genus orationis,; : mores,: vir ingenio sane probabili,.—Hence, adv.: prŏ-bābĭlĭter.
Probably, credibly (class.): rem breviter exponere et probabiliter,: rationem reddere,: dicere,: multa probabiliter argumentatus,: justius et probabilius accusare,: defendere,.—
Laudably, fitly, well (post-Aug.): consulatum gerere,: eleganter et probabiliter hoc dictum est,: recte et probabiliter dici,.—Comp.: probabilius Lutatius,.

la:noun:probatio.html:
prŏbātĭo, ōnis, f.
probo
.
A trying, proving; a trial, inspection, examination (class.): athletarum probatio,: futura,; : oesypi,: croci sinceri,: pumicis,: gemmae recusant limae probationem,: equitum,a review,.—
In partic.
Approbation, approval, assent (class.): ob probationem pretium datum,: tale visum nullum esse ut perceptio consequatur, ut autem probatio, multa,i. e. the assent of belief, though not the direct evidence of the senses,.—
Proof, demonstration (post-Aug.), : firma,: potentissimae,: ad cujus rei probationem immittit indices,: oculorum,ocular demonstration,.—
In partic., in rhet., the third part of a discourse, also called confirmatio or fides orationis, in which the orator enumerates his arguments, .

la:adj:probrus.html:
probrus, a, um, adj.
probrum
,
disgraceful, ignominious, infamous: animalia spurca atque probra,.

la:noun:probrum.html:
prŏbrum, i, n.
cf. Gr. προφέρειν, to reproach; and opprobrium
,
a shameful or disgraceful act (class.; syn.: dedecus, flagitium).
Lit.
In gen.: qui, nisi probrum, omnia alia indelicta aestimant, Att. ap. Müll.: flagitium probrumque magnum expergefacis,: ignaviae luxuriaeque probra,: emergere ex paternis probris ac vitiis,.—
In partic., unchaste or immodest conduct, lewdness, unchastity, adultery: Alcumenam insontem probri Amphitruo accusat,: exsequi,: vitii probrique plena,: probri insimulasti pudicissimam feminam,; : probri suspicio,; cf.: aliquam habere cum summo probro,; ; : probrum virginis Vestalis ut capite puniretur, Müll.—
Transf., the disgrace arising from an infamous act, shame, reproach, disgrace, dishonor, infamy: ea tum compressa parit huic puerum, sibi probrum, Caecil. ap. Müll.: nemo id probro ducet Alcumenae,: ego jam tua probra aperibo omnia,: in probro esse,: quem (Curium) censores senatu probri gratiā moverant,: vita rustica, quam tu probro et crimini putas esse oportere,to be reproachful, shameful,: postquam divitiae honori esse coeperunt, paupertas probro haberi,: probrum castis, labem integris, infamiam bonis inferre,: ut probrum objectare,: probrum atque dedecus,: terras implere probris,: luere sanguine probra,.—
In partic., abuse, insult, reproachful language, a reproach, libel: epistulae plenae omnium in me probrorum,: aliquem probris maledictisque vexare,: in isto tuo maledicto probrum mihi nullum objectas,: probra dicere alicui,: jactare in aliquem,: ingerere probra,: increpare multis ac servilibus probris,: probra jacere,: cumulare,: aggerare,: componere,: probris lacessere,: probris omnibus contaminatus,.

prŏbrōsus, a, um, adj.
probrum
,
shameful, ignominious, infamous (class.).
Of persons: vitā probrosus, et opertus infamiā,: feminae,: sordidissimus, et probrosissimus,.—
Of things: crimen,: o magna Carthago, probrosis Altior Italiae ruinis!: natura,: carmina,lampoons,: sermones,abusive discourses,: probrosae mollitiei homo,: compellationes,.—Adv.: prŏbrōsē,

disgracefully, infamously (postAug.): probrose leno illam prostituit,: obicere,.

la:noun:probabilitas.html:
prŏbābĭlĭtas, ātis, f.
probabilis
,
probability, credibility (class.): magna,: captiosa,: quodcumque nostros animos probabilitate percussit, id dicimus,.

la:noun:problema.gloss: problem, puzzle, enigma, question proposed for solution.
senses: problem, puzzle, enigma, question proposed for solution.
la:noun:problema.html:
problēma, ătis (
gen. plur. problematorum, ; abl. plur. problematis, ), n., = πρόβλημα, a question proposed for solution, a problem, enigma, riddle, puzzle (post-Aug.), : problemata φιλοσοφούμενα, : Aristotelis libri sunt, qui Problemata physica inscribuntur,: Aristoteles in septimo problematorum,; ; : in problematis Aristotelis,: proponam vobis problema,.—Hence, problēmătĭcus, a, um, adj., = προβληματικός, problematic; as subst.: problē-matĭca, ōrum, n., problems, cases set forth as problems (the title of a medical work), .

la:noun:probator.html:

id.
,

A trier, examiner (eccl. Lat.), .
